## How it works

- [statement] Lexmark identifies grain orientation as a contributor to card-stock rigidity and feed reliability. Grain must therefore be considered alongside stock weight when assessing a printing route. (low confidence) — https://publications.lexmark.com/publications/lexmark_hardware/Paper_and_Specialty_Media_Guide/html/en/GUID-394298ac-4ce2-42eb-ba93-90cebb822535-en.html
- [statement] Fedrigoni lists offset and screen printing among Symbol Card 2SC processes and lists varnishing and plastic lamination among converting processes; this is a process-specific manufacturer recommendation. (low confidence) — https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/SYMBOL-CARD-2SC-EN-1.pdf
- [statement] For the equipment addressed by its Color Materials Usage Guide, Xerox warns that coating chemistry can cause smearing, blurring or flaking in xerographic use even when the paper works in offset printing. (low confidence) — https://www.office.xerox.com/userdoc/DC4LP/pdfs/CMUG.pdf
- [statement] Xerox’s guide says excess paper moisture can produce fuser-related curl, while insufficient moisture can cause static; it recommends sealed, controlled storage and resealing opened reams. (low confidence) — https://www.office.xerox.com/userdoc/DC4LP/pdfs/CMUG.pdf
- [statement] Xerox’s guide says excessively rough texture can prevent dry ink from contacting the paper fully, leaving incomplete detail; the appearance of an embossed stock must therefore be checked with the intended xerographic process. (low confidence) — https://www.office.xerox.com/userdoc/DC4LP/pdfs/CMUG.pdf

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Fedrigoni’s April 2021 Symbol Card 2SC sheet lists its 300 g/m² board at 320 μm thickness, each ±5%, with Taber stiffness at 15° of 170 mN long direction and 120 mN cross direction, each ±15%; these figures describe this board, not all playing-card stocks. (low confidence) — https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/SYMBOL-CARD-2SC-EN-1.pdf
- [statement] Fedrigoni’s April 2021 sheet lists its 350 g/m² Symbol Card 2SC at 380 μm thickness, each ±5%, with Taber stiffness at 15° of 260 mN long direction and 170 mN cross direction, each ±15%. (low confidence) — https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/SYMBOL-CARD-2SC-EN-1.pdf

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PrintNinja states that its pre-textured linen stock cannot be laminated. This is a restriction of that supplier's stock and finishing combination. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-games/black-core-cardstock-for-board-games/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Grammage measures paper mass per area, rather than caliper: Fedrigoni defines grammage by square-metre weight and describes bulky papers as thicker at the same grammage. Specify finished thickness separately from GSM. (low confidence) — https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/glossary/
- [statement] MPC and PrintNinja describe black-core construction as a means of blocking transmitted light and improving card opacity. These are supplier descriptions, rather than independently measured opacity results for the proposed game. (medium confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/m31-linen-card-stock.aspx · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://printninja.com/custom-board-games/black-core-cardstock-for-board-games/
- [statement] MPC and QinPrinting describe a black center layer as an opacity feature that blocks light passing through paper playing cards; these are manufacturer descriptions rather than independent opacity measurements. (medium confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/m31-linen-card-stock.aspx · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://www.qinprinting.com/blog/how-to-choose-paper-and-surface-treatments-for-game-cards/
- [statement] GSM measures mass per area rather than thickness; Fedrigoni separately specifies substance, caliper and directional stiffness, so stock selection should retain these as separate specifications. (medium confidence) — https://www.supportivetarot.com/ultimate-guide-to-cardstock · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/SYMBOL-CARD-2SC-EN-1.pdf
- [statement] QinPrinting describes matte lamination as reducing glare and gloss lamination as reflective, with fingerprints more visible on dark gloss areas; these are vendor appearance claims rather than comparative measurements. (low confidence) — https://www.qinprinting.com/blog/how-to-choose-paper-and-surface-treatments-for-game-cards/
- [statement] Publisher Looney Labs reports that fresh cards can slide more because they are slicker, and that its more flexible stock held up to play; it treats perceived stiffness and durability as different properties rather than equating bendiness with poor quality. (low confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-materials-faq

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MPC describes embossed air pockets on its linen card surface; deck designer Mattgyver reports that linen texture helps cards shuffle and slide. The designer account is a qualitative handling assessment, without a measured friction or lifetime result. (medium confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/m31-linen-card-stock.aspx · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://www.mattgyver.com/tutorials/2022/3/14/playing-card-deck-design-tips
- [statement] PrintNinja describes film lamination as polypropylene applied to cards; it is a distinct material choice from the embossed linen texture. (medium confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-playing-cards/lamination-and-varnish-for-cards/ · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/m31-linen-card-stock.aspx
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that its anti-scratch matte lamination makes cards difficult to shuffle. Do not choose that finish for frequent shuffling solely for its matte appearance. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/custom-playing-cards/lamination-and-varnish-for-cards/
- [statement] Wizards of the Coast describes printed-card coatings as protection against moisture, scuffing and wear. This statement does not supply a waterproof rating or a measured service life. (low confidence) — https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/playing-card-coatings-2018-04-26
- [statement] In its 2018 manufacturing account, Wizards of the Coast describes its laminated playing-card paperboard as sensitive to humidity and temperature. Coating does not eliminate the need to evaluate environmental behaviour. (low confidence) — https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/playing-card-coatings-2018-04-26
- [statement] Looney Labs reports that its discussed newer stocks bend more easily than older stocks while holding up to play as well. This publisher observation scopes the assumption that a stiffer-feeling card necessarily lasts longer. (low confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-materials-faq
- [statement] Looney Labs warns that printing directly onto its blank cards may adhere poorly depending on the printer. A printable-looking card surface alone does not establish compatibility with a proposed press or ink system. (low confidence) — https://faq.looneylabs.com/non-gameplay-questions/game-materials-faq
- [statement] Wizards describes a matte finish as a way to reduce glare. That is a different property from the shuffling difficulty PrintNinja attributes to its anti-scratch matte film lamination; the word matte alone does not settle handling performance. (medium confidence) — https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/playing-card-coatings-2018-04-26 · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://printninja.com/custom-playing-cards/lamination-and-varnish-for-cards/
- [statement] MPC describes M31 linen as surface embossing with air pockets on both sides, and claims improved handling and durability; the claim does not establish a measured wear lifetime. (low confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/m31-linen-card-stock.aspx
- [statement] Symbol Card 2SC is described by Fedrigoni as double blade coated on both sides with a satin finish; its listed applications include packaging, covers and postcards. That specification alone does not establish playing-card shuffle feel. (low confidence) — https://specialpapers.fedrigoni.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/09/SYMBOL-CARD-2SC-EN-1.pdf
- [statement] Xerox’s Color Materials Usage Guide defines grain as fiber alignment and distinguishes grain-long from grain-short; it says folds run more smoothly with grain and cross-grain folds tend to crack. (low confidence) — https://www.office.xerox.com/userdoc/DC4LP/pdfs/CMUG.pdf
- [statement] Xerox’s guide warns that heavyweight duplexing can increase jams and degrade second-side image quality, and directs users to the machine-specific Recommended Materials list for duplex weight limits. (low confidence) — https://www.office.xerox.com/userdoc/DC4LP/pdfs/CMUG.pdf
- [statement] QinPrinting distinguishes film lamination after printing from liquid varnish, describing varnish as thinner and less moisture resistant than lamination; Lisa Papez’s guide also distinguishes liquid coatings from film-sheet lamination. (medium confidence) — https://www.qinprinting.com/blog/how-to-choose-paper-and-surface-treatments-for-game-cards/ · keywords: Paper card stocks cores coatings and handling · also: https://www.supportivetarot.com/ultimate-guide-to-cardstock
- [statement] QinPrinting describes poker varnish as a smooth low-friction coating for shuffling and dealing, and treats linen texture as a separate crosshatch treatment that can be combined with varnish. (low confidence) — https://www.qinprinting.com/blog/how-to-choose-paper-and-surface-treatments-for-game-cards/
- [statement] Reviewer Lisa Papez reports that her heavier decks can be harder to shuffle and that embossed coated linen can feel extra slippery; she recommends handling and shuffling physical samples before deciding on paper and finish. These are qualitative user observations, not controlled wear tests. (low confidence) — https://www.supportivetarot.com/ultimate-guide-to-cardstock
- [statement] MPC’s specifications page is internally inconsistent about S30: its overview calls the core black, while the detailed S30 paragraph calls it blue. The page does not resolve which description applies to an intended order. (low confidence) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/printed-card-types.aspx
